8e37ec89a058e3a46c1b9d2a72834771630f2827.summary: A malware analysis from The Safe Mac, reporting F-Secure's July 2013 announcement of Janicab, a trojan for Mac OS X. It disguises an application as a PDF using a right-to-left override character in the file name and is signed with a developer certificate, so it can run with little warning. Once run, it opens a decoy document, hides components in a folder in the home directory, sets a cron job, takes screenshots, records audio and polls a server for commands. At the time, most anti-virus software did not detect it. A July 16 update says the signing certificate appeared to be revoked.
